title: Projects
text:
Selected work
    Projects
    From my graduate studies, community leadership and work in procurement.
  



  
    
      
      
        01  /  DECISION ANALYSIS
        Bucka-Brew Investment Analysis
        AD 715 · Spring 2026 · Team project
        98% chance of at least $2.05M in profit over three years
        Financial modelingMonte Carlo simulationWhat-if analysisCorrelation analysis
        
          Details
          Context: A restaurant on Rainey Street in Austin asked whether to invest $175,000 in its own microbrewery.
          What I did:
          
            Built a 36-month financial model covering pricing, production and costs
            Tested buying versus renting brewing tanks. Buying 10 tanks came out about $24K ahead.
            Ran 10,000 simulations to stress-test profit against changing demand
          
          Result: Recommended the investment. It pays back in 9 months, with a 98% chance of at least $2.05M in profit over three years.
        
      
    
    
      
      
        02  /  SQL & PYTHON
        Northwind Traders Sales Analysis
        AD 599 · Summer 2026 · Team project
        One product drives 57.8% of Beverages revenue
        SQLWindow functionsPythonpandasSQLite
        
          Details
          Context: Our team analyzed a sales database for a fictional food distributor to find what drives revenue.
          What I did:
          
            Owned the product category analysis
            Ranked products within each category using SQL window functions, then ran the queries in Python
            Measured how much of each category's revenue comes from its top product
          
          Result: One product drives 57.8% of Beverages revenue, while Condiments is the most balanced at 15.8%. Categories that depend on one product carry more supply risk.
        
      
    
    
      
      
        03  /  BUSINESS ANALYTICS
        Riverdale Market Entry Strategy
        AD 571 · Spring 2026 · Individual · 5-part analysis
        An optimized entry plan with up to $773K in NPV and a $63K floor in a downturn
        Power BIRClusteringForecastingOptimization
        
          Details
          Context: A five-part analysis of whether a real estate firm should expand into Riverdale in the Bronx.
          What I did:
          
            Found prices at a five-year high of $514.70 per square foot (Power BI)
            Found prices are highly volatile (CV of 2.52), with few mid-market homes (R)
            Forecast about $63M in sales per quarter and showed that size, not age or season, drives price
            Built an optimization model to set the commission rate and staffing
          
          Result: Recommended entering lean with no new hires. That protects a $63K profit floor and keeps up to $773K in upside.
        
      
    
    
      
      
        04  /  TEAM PROJECT In progress
        Fashion & Apparel Career Evaluation
        AD 688 · Fall 2026 · Team project
        Power BI and SQL are the most requested skills (7 of 19 postings)
        PythonpandasPlotlyQuartoGitHub
        
          Details
          Context: Our team is building a research site on business and data analyst roles at apparel and fashion employers.
          What I did:
          
            Built the filtered industry dataset the team uses
            Cleaned the salary, experience, location and work-arrangement fields
          
          Early finding: Power BI and SQL are the most requested skills, each in 7 of 19 postings.
          View project site
        
      
    
    
      
      
        05  /  NONPROFIT LEADERSHIP
        Community Volunteer Impact Dashboard
        New York Junior League
        One view of volunteer hours, events and reporting across 25 committees
        Data visualizationKPI designSurvey analysis
        
          Details
          Context: Each committee reported volunteer hours differently, so leaders had no single view of impact.
          What I did:
          
            Built one dashboard of member volunteer hours and events across 25 committees
            Split direct service hours from meetings and prep
            Tracked which committees submitted monthly reports and which needed follow-up
            Summarized community partner survey feedback across three survey cycles
          
          Result: Council leaders can see where volunteer time goes and act on reporting gaps each month.
        
      
    
    
      
      
        06  /  PROCUREMENT ANALYTICS
        Meal Spend Analysis
        New York Junior League
        Created order-size rules for meal ordering and confirmed the best delivery provider
        Spend analysisFee analysisVendor strategy
        
          Details
          Context: Committee meal costs were rising, and the League wanted to know if it was ordering the right way.
          What I did:
          
            Analyzed a year of committee meal orders by size, fees and ordering method
            Confirmed our current delivery provider was still the lowest-fee option
            Found the catering option for large orders was rarely used
            Created order-size cutoffs from the analysis that tell committees when to use standard delivery, catering or a catering platform
          
          Result: The cutoffs became meal-ordering guidance for all committee co-chairs.

    Procurement spotlight
    Procurement Total Cost of Ownership Calculator
    Why it's here: Total cost of ownership is how I evaluate suppliers in my day job. I built this calculator to show the thinking behind a sourcing decision.
    Context: When choosing a supplier, the lowest price per unit isn't always the least expensive option. Total cost of ownership (TCO) measures what a supplier really costs over the full contract:
    TCO = Purchase price + Shipping + Import duties + Quality cost + One-time setup cost − Payment terms credit
    Enter two suppliers' details below to see which one actually costs less. Results update as you type.

    
      
        Annual volume (units)
        Contract term (years)
        Cost of capital (%)

        How it's calculated: Quality cost is the cost of replacing defective units. Payment terms credit is the value of keeping cash in the business longer when a supplier gives you more time to pay. It is calculated using your cost of capital. Sample values are shown; enter your own to compare.

title: Where procurement strategy meets analytics.
text:
Procurement  ·  Strategy  ·  Analytics
      Where procurement strategy meets analytics.
      I'm Alyssa, a global procurement leader who has built and scaled sourcing organizations across retail, consumer, and digital commerce brands. Today I lead Global Indirect Procurement at Ralph Lauren, and I'm working toward my MS in Applied Business Analytics at Boston University to build deeper analytics capabilities into how procurement operates.
      
        View my work
        Read my CV
      
    
    
      
    
  



  
    
      $2BAnnual spend managed
      $250M+Savings delivered
      6Global consumer brands
    
  



  
    
      Why analytics, why now
      Procurement has always run on data. It just hasn't always used it well.
    
    
      Procurement sits on some of the most valuable data in any company: every supplier, every contract, every dollar the business spends. However, in my experience, analytics remains one of the function's most underinvested capabilities. As a result, real value is left on the table because teams can't fully see what the data is telling them or act on those insights.
      Supply-chain volatility, cost pressure, and AI are changing how quickly organizations need to identify risk and take action. I went back to school to build the technical skills to put that data to work, including SQL, Spark, cloud platforms, and data visualization.
    
  



  
    What I bring
    Three lenses, one leader
    
      
        
        Strategic Sourcing
        Category strategy, supplier negotiation, and vendor management across apparel, accessories, and home and hardlines, plus indirect categories like marketing, technology, and logistics.
      
      
        
        Enterprise Transformation
        Standing up centralized procurement functions, procure-to-pay and ERP rollouts, M&A integration, and change management.
      
      
        
        Analytics & Insight
        Spend analysis, KPI frameworks, and dashboards, now backed by hands-on work in Python, SQL, Spark, R, and Power BI.
      
    
  



  
    Where I'm headed
    I want to lead procurement organizations where analytics is a core capability, not an afterthought: predictive spend insight, early supplier-risk signals, and decision tools that let teams move faster and with confidence.
  



  
    Brands I've built with
    
      TargetStarbucksTapestryRevlonFanaticsRalph Lauren
    
  



  
    
      
        Beyond the office
        Leading in the community
      
      
        As Community Senior Council Head with the New York Junior League, I oversee the committees in the League's Community area. These committees partner with organizations across New York City to improve the health and well-being of women, children and families. In my role, I'm working to better capture and report our volunteer engagement and community impact and bring the same process and data discipline I use at work to a mission I care about.
        I also serve on the Leadership Council of The Pink Agenda.
